children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after Federal Reserve Governor Michael S. Barr warned of leverage and circular-financing risks in artificial intelligence as the U.S. Commerce Department cracked down on overseas AI compute leasing.

In remarks published by the Federal Reserve, Barr said on-balance-sheet debt across the seven largest AI firms is expected to exceed $800 billion by year-end, while nominal off-balance-sheet leases and collateral guarantees surpass $3 trillion and circular equity stakes top $100 billion.

He cautioned that high hedge-fund leverage via dealer prime brokerage could fuel "self-reinforcing fire sales" during a repricing, alongside algorithmic conflicts steering clients toward proprietary products or higher transaction fees.

Separately, CNBC reported Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security will require licenses for advanced chips bound for Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil to block Chinese firms from leasing Nvidia compute abroad. That policy shift could complicate Wall Street’s AI deal pipeline.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Investment banking & brokerage company Interactive Brokers fell 4%.

children: XP’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 30 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

XP is down 8.9% since the beginning of the year, and at $14.75 per share, it is trading 54.8% below its 52-week high of $32.60 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of XP’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $455.80.
